title: Zechariah Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 12.

questions.question: What does the LORD form within man according to Zechariah 12:1?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD formeth the spirit of man within him, indicating the importance of the spirit in the creation of man.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:2, what will Jerusalem become to the people round about?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that Jerusalem will be made a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, highlighting its significance during sieges.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:3, what will happen to those who burden themselves with Jerusalem?
options: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, emphasizing the peril of opposing Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do to every horse in Zechariah 12:4?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will smite every horse with astonishment, indicating divine intervention.

questions.question: What shall the governors of Judah say in their heart according to Zechariah 12:5?
options: The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength
questions.explanation: The verse states that the governors of Judah shall say in their heart that the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be their strength in the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:6 states that Jerusalem will be inhabited again in her own place.
questions.explanation: The verse confirms that Jerusalem shall be inhabited again in her own place, affirming its restoration.

questions.question: True or False: In Zechariah 12:7, the LORD will save the tents of Judah last.
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD shall save the tents of Judah first, indicating priority in salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:8 compares the feeble among the inhabitants of Jerusalem to David.
questions.explanation: The verse states that the feeble among them shall be as David, illustrating their strength through divine support.

questions.question: What will happen to the nations that come against Jerusalem according to Zechariah 12:9?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:10, who will the inhabitants of Jerusalem look upon?
questions.explanation: The verse states they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, indicating a profound moment of recognition and mourning.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:11, how will the mourning in Jerusalem be described?
options: As the joy of the harvest
questions.explanation: The verse compares the mourning in Jerusalem to the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon, emphasizing its depth.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:12 states that every family will mourn apart.
questions.explanation: The verse confirms that every family shall mourn apart, indicating a personal and communal expression of grief.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:6 compare the governors of Judah to?
options: A hearth of fire and a torch of fire
questions.correctAnswer: A hearth of fire and a torch of fire
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:6 describes the governors as 'like a hearth of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire in a sheaf', indicating their strength and power in consuming the surrounding nations.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:10, who will the inhabitants of Jerusalem look upon?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 states that they 'shall look upon me whom they have pierced', which emphasizes the recognition of their wrong against the one who suffers for them.

questions.question: What will happen to Jerusalem according to Zechariah 12:3?
options: It will be a burdensome stone
It will be a place of peace
It will be a place of worship
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a burdensome stone
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:3 prophesies that Jerusalem will become 'a burdensome stone for all people', indicating that it will be a source of great challenge for those who oppose it.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:8 promise about the feeble among the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 12:8, it is promised that 'he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David', indicating that even the weak will be empowered.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:7, who will the LORD save first?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:7 states that 'The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first', demonstrating God's prioritization of Judah in His plan of salvation.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:4 say the LORD will smite?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:4 mentions that the LORD will 'smite every horse with astonishment', emphasizing divine intervention against the foes of Judah.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 12:9 demonstrate God's intention towards the nations against Jerusalem?
options: He will seek to destroy them
questions.correctAnswer: He will seek to destroy them
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 12:9, it is stated that 'I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem', indicating God's protective stance over His city.

questions.question: What will the families in the land do according to Zechariah 12:12?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:12 states that 'the land shall mourn, every family apart', highlighting a time of individual sorrow and reflection among the families.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:11 mentions a great mourning in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:11 states, 'In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem', confirming that mourning will indeed occur.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zechariah 12:10, the house of David will be in bitterness for him as one mourneth for his firstborn.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 describes the mourning for 'him, as one mourneth for his only son', indicating a profound grief similar to that of a parent for a firstborn.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:5 states that the governors of Judah shall rely on their own strength.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:5 indicates that the governors will say in their heart, 'The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength in the LORD of hosts their God', showing reliance on God rather than their own strength.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:3 imply about the consequences of opposing Jerusalem?
options: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:3 states that 'all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces', indicating severe consequences for those who oppose Jerusalem.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 12.

questions.question: What event is compared to the mourning in Jerusalem in Zechariah 12:11?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:11 states that there shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon, indicating the depth of sorrow expected.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:12, how will the land mourn?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:12 explicitly mentions that the land shall mourn, every family apart, indicating a personal and individual sense of loss.

questions.question: Which family is mentioned first in Zechariah 12:12 as mourning apart?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:12 states that the family of the house of David will mourn apart, showing their significance in this context.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:10, who will the inhabitants of Jerusalem look upon?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 indicates that the inhabitants of Jerusalem will look upon the one they have pierced, which is a foreshadowing of the passion of Christ as referenced in John 19:37.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Zechariah 12:10 when it mentions mourning?
questions.explanation: The mourning is compared to mourning for an only son, which is a simile used to evoke deep emotional resonance, as found in Zechariah 12:10.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:4, what will happen to the horses and their riders?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:4 states that the LORD will smite every horse with astonishment and its rider with madness, signifying divine intervention.

questions.question: Which family is mentioned in Zechariah 12:13 as mourning apart?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:13 mentions the family of the house of Levi mourning apart, indicating their distinct role in the context of mourning.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 12:3 states that Jerusalem will be a burdensome stone for all people.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:3 indicates that Jerusalem will be a burdensome stone for all people, confirming the statement as true.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:7 suggest about the order of salvation?
options: The glory of David will overshadow Judah
The tents of Judah will be saved first
questions.correctAnswer: The tents of Judah will be saved first
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:7 states that the LORD shall save the tents of Judah first, indicating a priority in divine intervention.

questions.question: True or False: The mourning mentioned in Zechariah 12:14 is depicted as collective and not individual.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:14 indicates that every family will mourn apart, highlighting that the mourning is individual rather than collective, making the statement false.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:6, how will the governors of Judah be likened?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:6 states that the governors of Judah will be like a hearth of fire among the wood, symbolizing their strength and power.

questions.question: Which verse speaks of the spirit of grace being poured upon the house of David?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 speaks explicitly of the LORD pouring the spirit of grace upon the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling' in Zechariah 12:2?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:2 indicates that Jerusalem will be a cup of trembling, pointing to the conflict and turmoil surrounding it.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:1 reveal about the nature of God?
options: He is only concerned with Israel
He has no power over nature
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:1 states that the LORD stretches forth the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth, demonstrating His role as Creator. This reflects God's sovereign authority over all creation, as seen in Genesis 1:1.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:2, what does the LORD declare Jerusalem will become for the surrounding peoples?
questions.explanation: The verse states that Jerusalem will become a cup of trembling for all people, indicating that it will be a source of distress for those who besiege it, reflecting God's judgment and protection over His people.

questions.question: What will happen to those who burden themselves with Jerusalem according to Zechariah 12:3?
options: They will be cut in pieces
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cut in pieces
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:3 states that all who burden themselves with Jerusalem shall be cut in pieces, highlighting the serious consequences of opposing God's chosen city.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:4, what will happen to the horses and their riders?
options: They will be smitten with astonishment
They will be blind to their surroundings
questions.correctAnswer: They will be smitten with astonishment
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:4 indicates that the LORD will smite every horse with astonishment and its rider with madness, revealing God's power to confound His enemies.

questions.question: What assurance do the governors of Judah find in Zechariah 12:5?
options: The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be their strength
They will be abandoned by God
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be their strength
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 12:5, the governors of Judah recognize that the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be their strength, indicating reliance on God’s power through the people.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:6 compare the governors of Judah to?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:6 compares the governors of Judah to a hearth of fire among wood, symbolizing their strength and ability to consume adversaries around them.

questions.question: In Zechariah 12:7, who does the LORD choose to save first?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:7 states that the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, indicating His priority in preserving His people before confronting their enemies.

questions.question: What transformation occurs for the feeble among the inhabitants of Jerusalem in Zechariah 12:8?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:8 promises that the feeble among the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be as David, indicating a divine empowerment that elevates their status and strength.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:10 predict the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will do?
options: Look upon Him whom they have pierced
questions.correctAnswer: Look upon Him whom they have pierced
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 foretells that they will look upon Him whom they have pierced, a clear foreshadowing of Christ's crucifixion and the mourning that follows.

questions.question: What event does Zechariah 12:11 compare the mourning in Jerusalem to?
options: The mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon
questions.correctAnswer: The mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:11 states there will be great mourning in Jerusalem as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon, illustrating the depth of sorrow and loss.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 12:12, how will the families mourn?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:12 describes that the land shall mourn, with every family mourning apart, indicating a deep, personal sorrow experienced individually despite collective grief.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 12:14 indicate about the mourning in Jerusalem?
options: It will be for every family apart
It will be ignored by outsiders
questions.correctAnswer: It will be for every family apart
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:14 confirms that all families that remain will mourn separately, reinforcing the theme of individual and collective grief in response to God's work.

questions.question: What sceptics claim about God's protection of Jerusalem in Zechariah 12:9?
options: God seeks to destroy all nations against Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God seeks to destroy all nations against Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Sceptics may claim God has abandoned Jerusalem, but Zechariah 12:9 teaches that God actively seeks to destroy all nations that come against it, affirming His protective stance.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Zechariah 12:10 and 12:11 convey about mourning?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 12:10 and 12:11 together illustrate that mourning is both a communal experience, as Jerusalem mourns, and a personal one, as families mourn apart.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is evident from the combination of Zechariah 12:7 and 12:8 regarding God’s salvation?
options: Salvation is only for the strong
God saves first and empowers His people
questions.correctAnswer: God saves first and empowers His people
questions.explanation: The combination of Zechariah 12:7, which discusses God saving Judah first, and 12:8, which emphasizes the empowerment of the feeble, shows God’s grace in saving and strengthening His people.
